section_summary: This section contains wartime Japanese food control statutes and postwar emergency regulations alongside 1947 U.S. diplomatic correspondence concerning civilian food relief and grain allocations for occupied Japan, Korea, and Germany. The Japanese legal texts (1940–1946) detail strict government distribution systems, compulsory delivery quotas, and expropriation procedures for staple crops including rice, wheat, and potatoes. The subsequent 1947 State and War Department records and Far Eastern Commission policy papers debate minimum caloric requirements and grain import priorities for Japan against competing European relief demands and limited U.S. exportable surpluses.

subfiles.about: Establishes distribution channels and accounting requirements for cereals through agricultural unions, control corporations, and the Japan Cereals Company.
subfiles.summary: Regulates the sale and consignment of cereals through authorized agricultural unions, control corporations, and the Japan Cereals Company, mandating strict transaction records and prefectural oversight.
subfiles.title: Regulations for Distribution Control of Cereals
subfiles.to: Prefectural governors, agricultural associations, and cereal dealers

subfiles.about: Establishes regulations for determining controlled rice quotas, affixing official certification marks to bags, and restricting unauthorized disposal of harvested rice.
subfiles.summary: Directs municipal agricultural associations to set controlled rice delivery quotas for producers and landlords, requires official certification marks on rice bags, and restricts unauthorized transfer or consumption.
subfiles.title: Appendix No. 31: Rice Control Regulations (Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry Ordinance No. 98)
subfiles.to: Prefectural governors, municipal agricultural associations, rice producers, and landowners

subfiles.about: Imposes rationing and shipment controls on wheat, barley, rye, and oats under the Law relating to the Control of Necessities of Life.
subfiles.summary: Controls distribution and consignment of wheat, barley, rye, and oats through local agricultural associations and the All-Japan Federation of Purchase and Sales Unions, prohibiting unauthorized sales or grain processing.
subfiles.title: Appendix No. 32: Wheat and Barley Distribution Control Regulations (Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry Ordinance No. 51)
subfiles.to: Agricultural associations, sales unions, and grain dealers

subfiles.about: Regulates the manufacture, pricing, and distribution of wheat flour and derivative products under the Vital Goods Ordinance.
subfiles.summary: Restricts flour manufacturing and sales to designated central and local distribution organs, preventing unauthorized milling by producers and enforcing statutory price ceilings.
subfiles.title: Appendix No. 33: Wheat Flour Distribution Control Regulations (Agriculture and Forestry Ministry Ordinance No. 58)
subfiles.to: Flour manufacturers and local distribution organs

subfiles.about: Establishes distribution controls, shipment planning, and commercial usage restrictions for potatoes, sweet potatoes, and root starches.
subfiles.summary: Directs distribution of potatoes and sweet potatoes through designated control organs and agricultural associations, setting mandatory shipment planning and restricting commercial processing and imports.
subfiles.title: Appendix No. 34: Potato Distribution Control Regulations
subfiles.to: Potato producers, agricultural associations, and designated control organs

subfiles.about: Regulates distribution, shipment, import, and custody of miscellaneous cereals including soybeans, beans, peas, and buckwheat.
subfiles.summary: Controls shipments and distribution of soybeans, peas, and buckwheat via agricultural associations and designated control organs, restricts soybean transport into the homeland, and appends an official inspection certificate form.
subfiles.title: Appendix No. 35: Miscellaneous Cereals Distribution Control Regulations (Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry Ordinance No. 91)
subfiles.to: Cereal producers, sales associations, and designated control organs

subfiles.about: Establishes comprehensive state control over staple food supplies, prices, distribution, and the creation of Central and Local Foodstuffs Corporations.
subfiles.summary: This foundational statute establishes comprehensive state control over the supply, demand, prices, and distribution of staple foodstuffs, including rice, barley, rye, and wheat. It mandates compulsory sales of staple foods by producers and landlords to the government at fixed prices and establishes the Central Foodstuffs Corporation (Chuo Shokuryo-eidan) and local foodstuffs corporations (Chiho Shokuryo-eidan) to manage storage and distribution. The law also restricts imports and exports, sets administrative and penal sanctions for violations, and repeals prior separate rice control statutes.
subfiles.title: Appendix No. 36: Foodstuff Control Law

subfiles.about: Empowers the Japanese government to expropriate staple foods from producers who fail to meet mandatory sales quotas and prescribes penalties for non-compliance.
subfiles.summary: Authorizes government officials to issue warrants and forcibly expropriate staple foods from farmers failing to fulfill delivery quotas, offering bond compensation and imposing prison sentences for obstruction.
subfiles.title: Appendix No. 37: Emergency Imperial Food Ordinance
subfiles.to: Staple food producers, administrators, and enforcement officials

subfiles.about: Outlines legal constraints and procedural safeguards preventing enforcement officials from using violence or unauthorized distraint during staple food expropriations.
subfiles.summary: Clarifies that food inspectors cannot use force to seize food, requiring referral to public procurators and judicial search warrants under the Code of Criminal Procedure.
subfiles.title: The Safeguards Against the Abuse of Authority by the Competent Official Concerned as Provided for in the Existing Laws

subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of the Joint War, State, and Agriculture Mission's report on food conditions in Japan, Korea, and the Ryukyus.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges receipt of the Joint Mission's report on food conditions in Japan, Korea, and the Ryukyus.
subfiles.title: Letter to Colonel R. L. Harrison regarding Joint Mission Report on Food Situation in Japan, Korea, and the Ryukyus
subfiles.to: Colonel R. L. Harrison, Assistant Administrator, Production and Marketing Administration, Department of Agriculture

subfiles.about: Transmits and analyzes a simplified United Kingdom draft policy paper on Japanese food relief submitted to the Far Eastern Commission.
subfiles.from: Roswell H. Whitman, Office of Economic Security Affairs
subfiles.summary: Transmits the UK draft food policy for Japan for War Department coordination, noting differences from FEC-026/12.
subfiles.title: Office Memorandum on Food Policy for Japan
subfiles.to: Mr. Rudlin, Division of Occupied Areas Economic Affairs

subfiles.about: Draft policy proposed by the United Kingdom setting strict limits on civilian food relief imports into Japan during the world food shortage.
subfiles.from: United Kingdom Delegation to the Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.summary: Recommends that food imports to Japan be limited to the minimum needed to prevent disease and unrest endangering occupation forces, without granting preferential treatment over Allied populations.
subfiles.title: Supply of Food for Civilian Relief in Japan (UK Draft Policy Paper)

subfiles.about: Circulates proposed United States amendments to the Far Eastern Commission draft policy on civilian food relief imports for Japan.
subfiles.from: Nelson T. Johnson, Secretary General, Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.summary: Circulates U.S. revisions restricting Japanese food imports to occupation safety needs while prohibiting priority over Allied or liberated nations.
subfiles.title: FEC-026/12: Supply of Food for Civilian Relief in Japan: Proposed United States Revision

subfiles.about: Explains the Department of State's decision declining to co-sign the Secretary of the Army's proposed letter requesting grain priorities for Japan and Korea.
subfiles.from: Philander P. Claxton, Jr., Acting Deputy to Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Declines to join the Army in requesting fixed grain priorities for Japan and Korea, citing U.S. export limits, German commitments, and unconfirmed harvest yields.
subfiles.title: Letter to Kenneth D. Johnson regarding Proposed Joint Letter on Grain Allocations for Japan and Korea
subfiles.to: Kenneth D. Johnson, Special Assistant to the Secretary of the Army

subfiles.about: Argues against supporting the War Department's request to guarantee 2.1 million metric tons of grain for Japan and Korea in fiscal year 1948.
subfiles.from: C. Tyler Wood, Office of Assistant Secretary for Economic Affairs
subfiles.summary: Recommends rejecting War Department grain requests for Japan and Korea, warning that fixed commitments threaten European needs and exceed export surplus margins.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Grain Shipment for Japan and Korea
subfiles.to: Philander P. Claxton, Jr., Acting Deputy to Assistant Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Transmits Secretary Royall's signed letter regarding Japanese and Korean grain requirements for Under Secretary Lovett's signature and dispatch.
subfiles.from: Kenneth D. Johnson, Special Assistant to the Secretary of War
subfiles.summary: Encloses Secretary Royall's signed letter on grain shipments, requesting Under Secretary Lovett's signature and prompt dispatch to Agriculture.
subfiles.title: Memorandum Transmitting Joint Letter to the Secretary of Agriculture
subfiles.to: Philander P. Claxton, Jr., Department of State

subfiles.about: Requests minimum fiscal year 1948 wheat deliveries of 1,700,000 metric tons for Japan and 400,000 metric tons for Korea to maintain minimum caloric rations.
subfiles.from: Kenneth C. Royall, Secretary of War, and Robert A. Lovett, Under Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Urges guaranteed delivery of 1.7 million tons of wheat for Japan and 400,000 tons for Korea to prevent severe disease.
subfiles.title: Proposed Joint Letter to the Secretary of Agriculture regarding Grain Allocations for Japan and Korea
subfiles.to: Clinton P. Anderson, Secretary of Agriculture

subfiles.about: Reviews disparate grain requirement estimates for Japan, Korea, and the Ryukyus, recommending a combined U.S. export target of 2,400,000 tons.
subfiles.from: Roswell H. Whitman, Office of Economic Security Affairs
subfiles.summary: Recommends allocating 2.4 million tons of grain to Japan, Korea, and the Ryukyus, opposing preferential treatment for Germany.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Food Requirements for Korea, Japan and Ryukyus - Fiscal Year 1948
subfiles.to: Paul H. Nitze, Office of International Trade Policy

subfiles.about: Defends the cereal allocation of 3,800,000 tons from the United States for the Bizonal area of Germany as essential to European economic recovery.
subfiles.from: John C. deWilde, Office of Economic Security Affairs
subfiles.summary: Defends Bizonal Germany's 3.8 million ton cereal allocation, arguing minimum rations are necessary to sustain European economic recovery.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Cereal Requirements of the US/UK Zones in Germany
subfiles.to: Paul H. Nitze, Office of International Trade Policy
